```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhou_2026_rituximab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhou_2026_rituximab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70683> (open access)

# Population

The model was developed from 45 treatment-naive Chinese adults with newly
diagnosed CD20-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) treated with
R-CHOP induction at a single centre (Third Affiliated Hospital of Soochow
University, September 2024 to October 2025), contributing 115 serum rituximab
concentrations. A further 12 patients (28 concentrations) were held out for
external validation. The modelling cohort (Table 1) was 16 male / 29 female,
aged 66.44 +/- 10.85 years, weighing 61.34 +/- 9.02 kg, with body surface area
1.76 +/- 0.14 m^2 and serum albumin-globulin (A/G) ratio 1.55 +/- 0.35
(interquartile range 1.33-1.66, Results). Rituximab was dosed at 375 mg/m^2
(500-750 mg per infusion) every 3 weeks, occasionally every 4 weeks, for 6-8
cycles, with a rate-escalated infusion. Samples were sparse clinical residuals
(pre-dose troughs and post-infusion samples) measured by chemiluminescence
immunoassay.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Zhou_2026_rituximab")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL at A/G 1.55) | 0.0181 L/h | Table 2; Eq 5 |
| `lvc` (V1) | 8.12 L | Table 2; Eq 6 |
| `lq` (Q) | 0.0213 L/h | Table 2; Eq 7 |
| `lvp` (V2) | 29.2 L | Table 2; Eq 8 |
| `e_alb_glob_ratio_cl` | -1.49 | Table 2 'A/G Ratio'; Eq 5 |
| A/G reference 1.55 | 1.55 | Eq 5 (= Table 1 cohort mean) |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.362^2) | Table 2 'IIV of CL (%)' 36.2; IIV on CL only (Results) |
| `propSd` | 0.316 | Table 2 'RV (%)' 31.6; proportional error (Methods) |
| CL = 0.0181 x exp(eta) x (A/G / 1.55)^-1.49 | n/a | Eq 5 |
| Two-compartment, first-order elimination, IV input | n/a | Methods, Base Model Development |

# Covariate effect and derived quantities

The steady-state volume (V1 + V2) is quoted in the Discussion as 37.32 L. The
clearance at the cohort A/G quartiles follows from Eq 5.

```{r covariate-effect}
mod <- readModelDb("Zhou_2026_rituximab")
pars <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta

cl_at <- function(ag) exp(pars[["lcl"]]) * (ag / 1.55)^pars[["e_alb_glob_ratio_cl"]]
vss <- exp(pars[["lvc"]]) + exp(pars[["lvp"]])

cl_tab <- tibble(
  `A/G ratio` = c(1.00, 1.33, 1.55, 1.66, 2.00),
  `CL from Eq 5 (L/h)` = signif(cl_at(c(1.00, 1.33, 1.55, 1.66, 2.00)), 3),
  `CL quoted in Results (L/h)` = c(NA, 0.0280, 0.0181, 0.0161, NA)
)
knitr::kable(cl_tab, caption = "Clearance across the A/G ratio range.")

stopifnot(
  abs(vss - 37.32) < 0.01,
  abs(cl_at(1.55) - 0.0181) < 1e-6
)
```

At the upper quartile (1.66) Eq 5 gives 0.0163 L/h against the quoted
0.0161 L/h. At the lower quartile (1.33) Eq 5 gives 0.0227 L/h, not the quoted
0.0280 L/h, and the quartile CL ratio is 1.39, not the "approximately
1.75-fold" in the Results and Discussion. No power, exponential or linear form
with the published coefficient reproduces both quoted values, so the model
follows Eq 5 and Table 2, which agree with each other and with the graphical
abstract (see Assumptions and deviations).

# Virtual cohort

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261114)
n_sub <- 200
n_cycles <- 6
tau <- 21 * 24 # h, standard 3-week cycle

# Rate-escalated infusion as consecutive constant-rate segments: start at r0
# mg/h, step up by `step` mg/h every 30 min, capped at rmax mg/h.
infusion_segments <- function(dose, r0, step, rmax, dt = 0.5) {
  off <- numeric(0)
  amt <- numeric(0)
  rate <- numeric(0)
  t_now <- 0
  remaining <- dose
  r <- r0
  while (remaining > 1e-9) {
    a <- if (r >= rmax) remaining else min(remaining, r * dt)
    off <- c(off, t_now)
    amt <- c(amt, a)
    rate <- c(rate, r)
    t_now <- t_now + a / r
    remaining <- remaining - a
    r <- min(r + step, rmax)
  }
  data.frame(off = off, amt = amt, rate = rate)
}

# A/G ratio: log-normal matched to the published interquartile range
# 1.33-1.66 (median 1.486, geometric SD from the IQR).
ag_sdlog <- log(1.66 / 1.33) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))
subjects <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  BSA = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 1.76, 0.14), 1.40), 2.20),
  ALB_GLOB_RATIO = exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(sqrt(1.33 * 1.66)), ag_sdlog))
) |>
  mutate(dose = pmin(pmax(375 * BSA, 500), 750))

dose_rows <- subjects |>
  tidyr::crossing(cycle = seq_len(n_cycles)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(seg = list(
    if (cycle == 1) infusion_segments(dose, 50, 50, 400) else infusion_segments(dose, 100, 100, 400)
  )) |>
  ungroup() |>
  tidyr::unnest(seg) |>
  transmute(id, time = (cycle - 1) * tau + off, amt, rate, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
            BSA, ALB_GLOB_RATIO)

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, n_cycles * tau, by = 12), (seq_len(n_cycles) - 1) * tau + 4)))
obs_rows <- subjects |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  transmute(id, time, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", BSA, ALB_GLOB_RATIO)

events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  mutate(regimen = "375 mg/m^2 q3w") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid", "amt")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("regimen", "ALB_GLOB_RATIO"),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = events |> filter(id == 1) |>
                             mutate(ALB_GLOB_RATIO = 1.55),
                           returnType = "data.frame")
```

# Concentration-time profile over induction

The paper presents goodness-of-fit and NPDE diagnostics (Figures 1-4) rather
than a VPC or a simulated profile, so there is no published figure to overlay.
The plot shows the simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles over six cycles,
with the typical-value profile at the reference A/G ratio and the 18.40 ug/mL
first-cycle trough threshold the paper compares against.

```{r profile, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
sim |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(data = sim_typ, aes(time / 24, Cc), linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 18.40, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Rituximab Cc (ug/mL)",
       title = "Simulated rituximab exposure over six R-CHOP cycles",
       caption = "Ribbon: 5th-95th percentile; dashed: typical value at A/G 1.55; dotted: 18.40 ug/mL.")
```

# First-cycle trough (Cmin,Cycle1)

The paper reports a median (range) first-cycle trough of 8.72 (0.19-17.23)
ug/mL from the empirical Bayes estimates of the 45 patients under the 21-day
interval, with all values below 18.40 ug/mL and the lowest troughs in patients
with A/G ratio below 1.

```{r trough}
trough1 <- sim |>
  filter(abs(time - tau) < 1e-6) |>
  select(id, Cc, ALB_GLOB_RATIO)

typ_trough <- sim_typ$Cc[abs(sim_typ$time - tau) < 1e-6]

trough_summary <- tibble(
  Quantity = c("Typical value at A/G 1.55", "Median of virtual cohort",
               "5th-95th percentile of virtual cohort", "Fraction below 18.40 ug/mL",
               "Published median (range), EBE-based"),
  Value = c(
    sprintf("%.2f ug/mL", typ_trough),
    sprintf("%.2f ug/mL", median(trough1$Cc)),
    sprintf("%.2f-%.2f ug/mL", quantile(trough1$Cc, 0.05), quantile(trough1$Cc, 0.95)),
    sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(trough1$Cc < 18.40)),
    "8.72 (0.19-17.23) ug/mL"
  )
)
knitr::kable(trough_summary, caption = "First-cycle trough, simulated vs. published.")

ggplot(trough1, aes(ALB_GLOB_RATIO, Cc)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 18.40, linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(x = "Albumin-globulin ratio", y = "Cmin,Cycle1 (ug/mL)",
       title = "First-cycle trough rises with the A/G ratio")

stopifnot(
  # Centre: the virtual-cohort median is within a factor of 1.5 of the
  # published EBE median (different cohorts, so not a tight match).
  median(trough1$Cc) > 8.72 / 1.5,
  median(trough1$Cc) < 8.72 * 1.5,
  # Direction of the covariate effect: troughs correlate positively with A/G.
  cor(trough1$ALB_GLOB_RATIO, trough1$Cc, method = "spearman") > 0.2
)
```

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, regimen) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, regimen, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, regimen, time)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(cycle_start = floor(time / tau) * tau) |>
  group_by(id, regimen, time = cycle_start) |>
  summarise(amt = sum(amt), .groups = "drop")

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id, route = "intravascular")

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 5 * tau),
  end = c(tau, 6 * tau),
  cmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE,
  ctrough = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  group_by(start, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Interval = ifelse(start == 0, "Cycle 1 (0-21 d)", "Cycle 6 (105-126 d)")) |>
  select(Interval, PPTESTCD, median) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
nca_tab |>
  rename(any_of(c("Cmax (ug/mL)" = "cmax", "AUClast (ug*h/mL)" = "auclast",
                  "Ctrough (ug/mL)" = "ctrough", "Cmin (ug/mL)" = "cmin"))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters per dosing interval.")

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~ctrough,
  "375 mg/m^2 q3w", 8.72
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "regimen",
  units = c(ctrough = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published first-cycle trough (median). * differs by >20%.")
```

The simulated cohort median (`r sprintf("%.1f", median(trough1$Cc))` ug/mL)
sits above the published median of 8.72 ug/mL. The published value is the median of empirical Bayes
predictions for the 45 real patients, whose A/G distribution has a heavier
lower tail (mean 1.55, SD 0.35, with several patients below 1) than the
log-normal fitted here to the interquartile range; the virtual cohort is not a
reconstruction of those patients, and the parameters are not tuned to close the
gap. The typical-value trough at the reference A/G ratio and the
direction and size of the A/G effect follow directly from Table 2.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Quartile clearances in the Results.** The Results quote CL of about
  0.0280 L/h and 0.0161 L/h at the A/G quartiles 1.33 and 1.66 (a 1.75-fold
  range). Eq 5 with the Table 2 exponent -1.49 gives 0.0227 and 0.0163 L/h
  (1.39-fold). The equation, Table 2 and the graphical abstract agree, so the
  model follows them; the quoted quartile values could not be reproduced.
- **A/G ratio column.** The paper does not state whether the A/G ratio was
  carried as a baseline or a per-cycle value; the model accepts either.
- **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV on CL as 36.2% without a CV definition;
  with the log-normal IIV stated in the Methods it is converted as
  `log(1 + 0.362^2)`. IIV was estimated on CL only (Results).
- **Residual error.** Table 2 'RV (%)' 31.6 is taken as the proportional
  residual SD (0.316), per the proportional error model in the Methods.
- **Virtual cohort.** BSA ~ normal(1.76, 0.14) truncated to 1.40-2.20 m^2;
  dose 375 mg/m^2 limited to 500-750 mg; A/G ratio log-normal matched to the
  published interquartile range. Six 21-day cycles; the paper allows 6-8 cycles
  and occasional 28-day intervals.
- **Infusion.** The rate-escalation schedule in the Methods (first infusion
  50 mg/h rising by 50 mg/h every 30 min to 400 mg/h; later infusions starting
  at 100 mg/h rising by 100 mg/h every 30 min) is encoded as consecutive
  constant-rate infusion segments. Interruptions for infusion reactions are not
  modelled.
- **Linear model.** The authors note that sparse retrospective sampling
  precluded a TMDD model, so CL is an apparent value that may mix linear and
  target-mediated clearance, and V1 is likely overestimated because peaks were
  not captured (Discussion).
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article as of 2026-11-14.
